Thanks Karthik — good summary. A few clarifications from AP/Procurement side: 

- For pilots under $15k we typically allow corporate card payments. Anything over $15k requires a PO. Our pilot forecast (based on your estimate) looks like it might land in the $18–22k range for the first month, so likely will need a PO unless we reduce scope.
- Vendor onboarding: we will need a completed W-9 (for US vendors), a supplier setup form (PDF), and proof of insurance for vendor-hosted services if applicable. Once we get the paperwork the standard timeline is ~10 business days to onboard and issue a PO.
- Marketplace: we are evaluating Marketplace procurement, but our internal Marketplace listing is only available for SaaS vendors that pass an additional security review. That review can add ~2–3 weeks unless the vendor already has a SOC2 report and shared compliance artifacts.

I attached our AP policy for reference (Aurora_AP_Policy.pdf).

Preferred next step: Please have Redwood share the vendor onboarding packet and a one-page commercial summary (SOW estimate + billing cadence) so I can share with our procurement team. If possible, please include a ballpark invoice schedule we can use to estimate monthly spend.

Hi Samira — thanks for the clear note and for sharing the AP policy. Welcome — excited to partner on this pilot. Quick runbook from Redwood procurement + suggested timeline: 

What we can provide now (attached):
- Redwood_Vendor_Onboarding_Packet.pdf (supplier setup form, W-9 template, required fields)
- Redwood_PO_Instructions.pdf (how to format PO, billing contact, remit address, PO email + DocuSign instructions)

Typical onboarding timeline:
1) Customer returns completed onboarding packet + W-9 & supplier fields → | Day 0
2) Redwood finance validates docs and performs tax/identity checks → Day 1–3
3) Finance creates vendor record and issues vendor ID → Day 3–7
4) Once vendor record is created, PO issuance and acceptance → Day 7–12

So ~7–12 business days total is typical. If Aurora wants faster access for the pilot we can support a temporary invoice-based pilot (corporate card charge or advance invoice) for the first 30 days while PO is processed; that requires a signed SOW and purchase order to be submitted within 30 days to convert to standard billing. 

PO formatting notes (short):
- Include Redwood vendor legal name: Redwood Inference, Inc.
- Please include our remit address and vendor ID (provided once vendor record created).
- Net 30 default; for pilot billing cadence we can accept milestone billing (monthly) if noted on the PO.

Action items:
- Karthik: send the 1‑page SOW with estimated monthly spend and preferred billing cadence.
- Samira/Daniel: return the completed onboarding packet + W-9 (scan OK) or confirm if you want to run pilot on card and provide card authorization.
- Ben: if they need a temporary credit arrangement, can you confirm maximum advance invoice we can entertain for pilots?
